title: Androgen receptor signaling in hepatocellular carcinoma: mechanisms of male predominance and therapeutic opportunities.
abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is two to four times more common in men than in women. The sex distribution of viral hepatitis, alcohol use and adiposity explains only part of this difference, which points to sex-specific host biology as a further driver. The androgen receptor (AR), a ligand-activated transcription factor expressed in hepatocytes and in most HCC, is a strong candidate: both epidemiologic and experimental data implicate it in the male excess. This review draws that evidence together. Prospective cohorts link higher circulating testosterone and sex hormone-binding globulin to liver cancer risk, although raising SHBG experimentally suppresses rather than promotes hepatocarcinogenesis, a discordance that bears on how those associations should be read, and experimental studies group the underlying biology into several modules: constitutively active AR and its splice variants, kinase-driven phosphorylation of the receptor, downstream effectors of proliferation, invasion and angiogenesis, non-coding RNA circuits, androgen-metabolizing enzymes and the systemic endocrine axis, and the effect of androgen on the tumor immune microenvironment. The weight of each module differs across hepatitis B virus (HBV)-related, hepatitis C virus (HCV)-related, metabolic dysfunction-associated and anabolic steroid-induced disease. Therapeutic work remains largely preclinical and has centered on AR antagonists combined with tyrosine kinase inhibitors or immune checkpoint blockade, on degraders aimed at AR splice variants, on proteolysis-targeting chimeras and nucleic-acid approaches that eliminate ligand-independent receptor states, and on enzyme inhibitors. Two problems still limit translation: AR appears oncogenic in most settings but tumor-suppressive in some, and androgen suppresses antitumor immunity in certain contexts while enhancing it in others. Clarifying when each holds is what will determine whether AR-directed therapy, already established in prostate cancer, can be extended to liver cancer.

title: Regorafenib induces ferroptosis in hepatocellular carcinoma via the EGFR-TNF/NF-κB signaling axis.
abstract: Regorafenib is a standard second-line multi-targeted tyrosine kinase inhibitor for sorafenib-resistant hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). Ferroptosis is a promising therapeutic cell-death modality, but the upstream signaling events governing regorafenib-induced ferroptosis remain unclear. We examined regorafenib activity in treatment-naive SNU-449 and HuH-7 HCC cells and mouse tumor models using ferroptosis-related assays, including reactive oxygen species (ROS), malondialdehyde (MDA), labile Fe2+, lipid peroxidation and mitochondrial ultrastructure. Transcriptome profiling was integrated with genetic and pharmacological modulation of EGFR and p65. Antitumor effects were assessed in HuH-7 xenografts and Hepa1-6 syngeneic tumors. Regorafenib suppressed proliferation, migration, invasion, and tumor growth, with reduced Ki-67 expression. It downregulated SLC7A11/xCT and glutathione peroxidase 4 (GPX4) and increased ROS, labile Fe2+, lipid peroxidation, and MDA; ferrostatin-1 partially restored viability and attenuated lipid peroxidation. Transcriptome analysis identified enrichment of the TNF signaling pathway. Regorafenib reduced total and phosphorylated EGFR and p65, decreased the p-EGFR/EGFR and p-p65/p65 ratios, and inhibited p65 nuclear translocation. p65 knockdown decreased SLC7A11/xCT and GPX4 and intensified ferroptosis, whereas p65 overexpression attenuated these effects. EGFR knockdown reduced TNF-α and enhanced ferroptosis; the EGFR agonist NSC228155 restored NF-κB activity and SLC7A11/xCT-GPX4 expression. Combined EGFR knockdown and lenalidomide treatment further enhanced ferroptosis-associated phenotypes in vitro. Exploratory analysis of 24 paired specimens showed EGFR, p65, and GPX4 were upregulated and positively associated. These findings identify EGFR-TNF/NF-κB signaling as a functional upstream module in treatment-naive HCC models and support validating combined EGFR knockdown and lenalidomide treatment in resistant models.
journal: Apoptosis : an international journal on programmed cell death

title: Redox shielding unlocks damage-free photopolymerization for GelMA 3D co-cultures mimicking pancreatic tumor complexity.
abstract: Developing physiologically relevant 3D tumor models is critical to study cell-stroma interactions driving cancer progression. In pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC), pancreatic stellate cells (PSCs) are key stromal actors that acquire pro-tumoral functions upon activation into cancer-associated fibroblasts (CAFs). We aimed to create a 3D co-culture model combining PSCs (or CAFs) and tumor organoids (or spheroids) that reproduces the tumor microenvironment while preserving the viability of fragile stroma cells. Gelatin methacryloyl (GelMA) was selected as a biocompatible scaffold with mechanical properties comparable to pancreatic tissue. However, fragile stromal cells, such as PSCs, displayed extensive photopolymerization-induced cell death when embedded in GelMA, preventing long-term culture. We developed a simple preconditioning protocol with an antioxidant (N-acetylcysteine, NAC) that protects sensitive cells prior to GelMA encapsulation. This approach allowed long-term 3D culture of healthy PSCs and CAFs, alone or in co-culture with tumor spheroids or organoids. Cells self-organized, maintained physiological morphology, secreted extracellular matrix, and formed stromal networks around tumor structures, closely mimicking the PDAC tissue architecture. This straightforward and reproducible approach enables sensitive stromal cells to thrive in 3D GelMA, providing a robust platform to study tumor-stroma crosstalk and to support drug testing in PDAC-relevant models.

title: Integrated single-cell and proteomic profiling of pancreatic neoplasia identifies tissue markers that outperform established diagnostic markers in distinguishing cancer from precursor lesions.
abstract: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) arises within an extensively remodeled microenvironment, yet tissue markers that distinguish invasive carcinoma from precursor lesions remain limited. Integrating four single-cell RNA-sequencing atlases comprising 324,662 cells from 26 patients, we identified cancer-associated fibroblast expansion, accumulation of C1QA+ immunoregulatory macrophages, and depletion of a dendritic-cell compartment expressing plasmacytoid markers. Fibroblasts were enriched for extracellular-matrix and PI3K-AKT programs and macrophages for an antigen-presentation program. We then examined the protein-level correlates of these populations in a tissue proteomic reference framework of 356 samples spanning non-diseased pancreas, normal-adjacent tissue, low- and high-grade intraductal papillary mucinous neoplasms (IPMNs), IPMN-associated invasive carcinoma, and PDAC, prioritizing proteins that changed monotonically across the six histopathologic reference groups or marked tumor-enriched cell types. Despite depletion of plasmacytoid dendritic cells, the principal source of type I interferon, the interferon-stimulated protein ISG15, expressed by both fibroblasts and macrophages, increased monotonically toward PDAC. In exploratory cross-validated benchmarking of PDAC versus low- and high-grade IPMN, excluding IPMN-associated invasive carcinoma (145 versus 56 samples), CATB+EPIPL achieved an AUC of 0.98, with a sensitivity of 92% at an achieved specificity of 92%, exceeding protein-abundance models of diagnostic IHC-associated markers (S100P+IMP3+maspin+MSLN, 0.79) and refitted published IPMN-progression combinations (≤0.91). Against non-diseased pancreas, candidate and comparator panels performed similarly (AUC 0.99-1.00). These biologically informed tissue protein panels warrant independent validation, including immunohistochemical evaluation of EUS-guided fine-needle biopsy specimens and measurement in blood.
journal: medRxiv : the preprint server for health sciences

title: HMGA2 Expression in Pancreatic Ductal Adenocarcinoma Controls Tumor Microenvironment and Immunosuppression via IL1α.
abstract:
UNLABELLED: The basal-like subtype of pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) is associated with poor outcomes and increased chemoresistance. Expression of high mobility group AT-hook 2 (HMGA2), a chromatin architectural protein, marks basal PDAC cells and associates with specific features of the tumor microenvironment (TME), including more immunosuppressive cancer associated fibroblasts (CAFs) and fewer cytotoxic CD8 + T cells. Expression of HMGA2 by tumor cells leads to upregulation of the immunosuppressive markers interleukin 6 (IL6) and leucine-rich repeat containing protein 15 (LRRC15) in associated fibroblasts. Mechanistically, HMGA2 in the tumor cell binds the interleukin 1 alpha (IL1α) promoter and upregulates transcription, increasing IL1α in the TME, in turn inducing immunosuppressive fibroblast polarization, increasing regulatory T cells, and decreasing CD8 + T cells. Blockade of the IL1α signaling axis disrupts this tumor-driven microenvironment phenotype and combines with inhibitors of oncogenic KRAS to improve tumor control.
STATEMENT OF SIGNIFICANCE: The tumor microenvironment of pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma drives immunosuppression, but causal relationships between PDAC subtypes and the TME have not been established. We report direct regulation of IL1α signaling by a basal PDAC-specific factor that controls fibroblast polarization and drives immunosuppression.
journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology

title: Immunopharmacological Advances in HBV Associated Hepatocellular Carcinoma and EBV-Related Nasopharyngeal Carcinoma in China: Mechanisms, Therapies, and Clinical Perspectives.
abstract: Oncogenic viruses continue to be a significant cause of cancer in China, with a significant proportion of malignancies caused by hepatitis B virus (HBV) and Epstein-Barr virus (EBV). HBV is the dominant etiological factor for HCC in China, accounting for approximately 85-92% of cases. EBV is closely implicated in non-keratinizing undifferentiated nasopharyngeal carcinoma (NPC), especially in endemic areas. The use of conventional treatment methods, such as surgery, radiotherapy, and chemotherapy, has not been very effective, especially at advanced stages of the disease, underscoring the need to incorporate more effective treatment approaches. Immunopharmacological interventions have emerged as a revolutionary practice in this regard. This review provides an overview of existing immunopharmacology in HBV-related HCC and EBV-associated NPC, including how the tumour immune microenvironment is modulated, the mechanisms of action of immune-based therapies, and the major clinical advances in China. Domestically developed anti-PD-1 antibodies, such as sintilimab, camrelizumab, tislelizumab, and toripalimab, have received regulatory approval based on large-scale clinical trials and are currently used as first-line treatment for unresectable HCC and for recurrent or metastatic NPC. Simultaneously, adoptive cellular therapies using EBV antigens (including EBV-specific cytotoxic T lymphocytes and engineered T-cell receptor strategies) have shown promising clinical potential. Moreover, combination regimens with immune checkpoint blockade and targeted therapies or locoregional therapies have demonstrated better survival rates, especially in HBV-infected people. Despite these improvements, there are still issues, such as therapeutic resistance, immune-related adverse events, and inconsistent biomarker performance. Future initiatives must focus on biomarker-directed treatment decisions, combination regimen optimization, and the wider clinical use of new cellular therapies.

title: Erianin Targets Glutathione Reductase to Trigger Immunogenic Cell Death and Sensitize Pancreatic Cancer to PD-1 Blockade.
abstract: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) responds poorly to immune checkpoint blockade (ICB), largely because of its immunosuppressive and T-cell-excluded tumor microenvironment. While inducing immunogenic cell death (ICD) offers a promising strategy to enhance tumor immunogenicity, redox-targeted ICD inducers with defined molecular targets remain limited in PDAC. Here, a functional screen of natural compounds identified erianin as a potent ICD inducer in PDAC. Erianin triggered canonical ICD hallmarks, including cell-surface calreticulin exposure, extracellular release of HMGB1 and ATP, thereby promoting dendritic-cell maturation, antigen cross-presentation and CD8+ T-cell activation. Target-engagement assays together with genetic perturbation supported glutathione reductase (GSR) as a functionally important erianin target. Erianin decreased the GSH/GSSG ratio, accompanied by increased oxidative stress and preferential activation of the PERK-eIF2α-ATF4-CHOP branch of the endoplasmic reticulum (ER) stress response. Mutational and rescue experiments identified residue ARG-233 as an important residue required for GSR-dependent protection against erianin-induced redox stress and ICD. In syngeneic PDAC models, erianin-treated tumor cells elicited protective antitumor immunity in a tumor-challenge setting, while a therapeutic regimen combining erianin with anti-PD-1 antibody suppressed tumor growth and was associated with increased dendritic-cell activation and enhanced cytotoxic CD8+ T-cell infiltration. These findings define a GSR-associated redox-immune axis that links glutathione metabolism to immunogenic ER stress and provide a rationale for combining erianin with PD-1 blockade in immunologically cold PDAC.

title: Gallbladder cancer beyond genetics: tumor-immune microenvironment interactions and emerging translational therapeutic strategies.
abstract: Gallbladder cancer (GBC) is an aggressive malignancy where tumor-intrinsic genomic alterations fail to fully explain its rapid invasiveness and therapeutic resistance. Unlike more generic reviews focused broadly on biliary tract cancers or limited to isolated genomic profiling, this review provides an in-depth dissection of the GBC tumor microenvironment (TME) as an integrated tumor-immune-stromal-neural ecosystem. Key microenvironmental drivers are illuminated, including cancer-associated fibroblast remodeling, immunosuppressive myeloid reprogramming, T-cell dysfunction, and neuro-tumor crosstalk driving perineural invasion. Crucially, this review establishes a structured evidence hierarchy that rigorously distinguishes GBC-specific findings from broader biliary cohorts and tumor-agnostic data. By synthesizing multimodal computational frameworks and microenvironment-directed combination strategies, this review provides an actionable precision oncology roadmap to overcome therapeutic resistance and improve patient outcomes in GBC.
journal: Biochimica et biophysica acta. Reviews on cancer

title: TACE and yttrium 90 based combination therapies are associated with distinct post-treatment tumor microenvironment profiles in unresectable hepatocellular carcinoma.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: The direct comparisons between transarterial chemoembolization (TACE) and Yttrium-90 (Y-90) radioembolization in combination with systemic therapies to treat unresectable hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) are lacking, and the distinct impacts of these combination therapies on the tumor microenvironment (TME) have not been investigated. The aim of this study was to directly compare the clinical efficacy and post-treatment TME profiles between TACE and Y-90 plus systemic therapies.
METHODS: A total of 210 patients with unresectable HCC were included and divided into 2 groups: TACE + systemic therapies (n = 159) and Y-90 + systemic therapies (n = 51). Baseline characteristics and clinical outcomes between these 2 groups were compared. Furthermore, TME profiles after TACE + systemic therapies and Y-90 + systemic therapies were analyzed by single-cell RNA sequencing. Besides, the multiplex immunofluorescence was conducted to verify these TME characteristics.
RESULTS: Y-90 + systemic therapies group showed significantly higher disease control rate and conversion rate compared to TACE + systemic therapies group (p < 0.05). Also, Y-90 + systemic therapies showed higher progression-free survival and overall survival compared to TACE + systemic therapies (p < 0.05). Notably, single-cell transcriptomic analysis revealed that Y-90 + systemic therapies was associated with a more immune-activated TME, characterized by reduced T cell exhaustion, a lower proportion of regulatory T cells and enrichment of immune activation and chemotaxis pathways.
CONCLUSIONS: Y-90 + systemic therapies was associated with favorable clinical outcomes and distinct post-treatment tumor microenvironment characteristics. These findings provide exploratory insights into potential biological differences between Y-90 and TACE-based combination strategies.

title: IL-37 links ACLY-centered lipid metabolic reprogramming to myeloid immunosuppression in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma.
abstract: This study investigated the role of IL-37 in PDAC and its association with lipid metabolic reprogramming and tumour immune suppression. Bioinformatic analyses, paired clinical specimens, IL-37 gain- and loss-of-function models, and in vitro and in vivo functional assays were used to characterize the role of IL-37 in PDAC. Tumour immune profiles and metabolic alterations were assessed by flow cytometry, immunofluorescence, molecular analyses, and untargeted metabolomics. Bone marrow-derived MDSC assays and pharmacological AKT inhibition were used for mechanistic validation, and the effects of ACLY inhibition and Gr-1 blockade were further evaluated in vivo. IL-37 was upregulated in PDAC tissues and cell lines and was associated with shorter overall survival. IL-37 overexpression enhanced cell viability, clonogenicity, migration, invasion, and tumour growth, whereas IL-37 knockdown produced the opposite effects. IL-37 overexpression was also associated with increased CD11b+Gr-1+ myeloid-derived suppressor cell accumulation and impaired CD8+ T-cell infiltration. Tumour-derived IL-37-associated signals further promoted MDSC generation and preferentially shifted the population toward M-MDSCs in vitro. Metabolomic and molecular analyses revealed an ACLY-centred lipid metabolic programme involving increased ACLY, FASN, and SPHK1 expression and alterations in acetyl-CoA, palmitate, and sphingosine-1-phosphate. IL-37 enhanced AKT phosphorylation, whereas AKT inhibition attenuated the upregulation of ACLY, FASN, and SPHK1, supporting a functional role for AKT signalling in this metabolic phenotype. ACLY inhibition, particularly in combination with Gr-1 blockade, reduced lipid accumulation and myeloid-cell infiltration, restored CD8+ T-cell responses, and suppressed tumour growth. IL-37 promotes PDAC progression in association with AKT-related signalling, ACLY-centred lipid metabolic reprogramming and an immunosuppressive tumour microenvironment. Combined targeting of lipid metabolism and immunosuppressive myeloid cells may represent a therapeutic strategy for IL-37-high PDAC.

title: HBV PreS Variants Significantly Decrease in Liver Tissues After 104 Weeks of Antiviral Therapy With Nucleos(t)ide Analogues.
abstract: Nucleos(t)ide analogues (NAs) are widely used in patients infected with hepatitis B virus (HBV). However, limited data are available on the changes of the HBV variants at 2 years (104 weeks, w) after therapy, largely due to the difficulty in detecting the viral genome in peripheral blood. In our study, fifteen HBV-infected patients (HBV e antigen positive) were enrolled, liver biopsy was performed at baseline and 104 w to evaluate liver fibrosis, and the clinically significant HBV variants related to hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) and viral quasispecies diversity were also analyzed. PreS deletions were found in eight patients (53.3%) at baseline. All the eight patients showed a decrease in preS deletions after antiviral therapy (p < 0.05). Moreover, all the eight patients with the preS2 start codon mutations/deletions at baseline were decreased after NAs treatment. BCP/preC mutations did not significantly change among the patients, including the eight patients achieved HBeAg seroconversion (all p > 0.05). HBV quasispecies diversity did not show significant differences, and no NAs-related drug resistance mutations were found in the eight patients with low-level viremia. The reduction of HBV preS variants may represent one of the important mechanisms by which NAs therapy lowers the risk of progression to HCC.

title: scGlycoAI: Machine learning analysis of single-cell glycan and RNA sequencing data for cell-type annotation and malignancy-associated glycan discovery.
abstract: Single-cell glycan and RNA sequencing (scGR-seq) enables characterization of cellular glycan heterogeneity. Here, we present scGlycoAI, an interpretable machine learning framework that integrates scGR-seq data for glycan-centered biological discovery. Using lectin-binding profiles as input, scGlycoAI employs hierarchical machine learning to accurately classify cell types and subtypes within complex tumor microenvironments. Applied to pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) datasets, scGlycoAI achieved an overall eight-class classification accuracy of 90.3% under leave-one-patient-out validation using glycan features alone. These results demonstrate that glycan signatures, despite their lower dimensionality compared with transcriptomic profiles, are sufficient for robust cell-type annotation and represent cell-type-specific molecular signatures. Feature importance analysis identified PVL lectin binding, which reflects recognition of sialylated and/or GlcNAc-containing glycans, as a key feature of aggressive cancer states. A neural-network model combined with SHAP-based interpretation further revealed that elevated PVL binding was associated with transcriptional programs linked to epithelial-mesenchymal transition, KRAS signaling, extracellular matrix remodeling, and inflammatory responses. Higher expression of the PVL-associated gene signature was associated with poorer overall survival in the TCGA pancreatic adenocarcinoma cohort. Collectively, these findings suggest that glycan-based machine learning enables accurate cell classification while providing biological insights into malignancy-associated glycan states at single-cell resolution. This framework provides a foundation for glycan-centered biomarker discovery and glycan-targeted therapeutic development.

title: Glycosylated Hypoxic Tumor-Derived Extracellular Vesicles as a Targeted siRNA Delivery System to Remodel the Immunosuppressive Microenvironment in Pancreatic Cancer.
abstract: GalNAc-modified extracellular vesicles (EVs) derived from hypoxic pancreatic cancer cells and loaded with ANXA2 siRNA were developed to modulate the immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment (TME). Characterization confirmed successful surface modification and efficient siRNA loading in EVs with a diameter of approximately 100-120 nm. In vitro, these engineered EVs inhibited pancreatic cancer cell proliferation, migration, and invasion and promoted apoptosis. Additional cargo-matched comparison showed that GalNAc-modified hypoxic EVs carrying ANXA2 siRNA produced stronger ANXA2 silencing and more pronounced anti-migratory, anti-invasive, and pro-apoptotic effects than unmodified hypoxic EVs carrying the same siRNA, whereas GalNAc modification alone did not show an obvious independent antitumor effect. In a xenograft model, treatment reduced tumor volume by approximately 50% at week 4 and prolonged median survival from 45 to 60 days. Multi-omics and immune analyses suggested suppression of the PI3K/AKT signaling pathway and remodeling of the immunosuppressive TME, as reflected by increased CD8+ T-cell infiltration, reduced tissue-associated immunoreactivity for IL-6, IL-10, and TNF-α, and increased soluble IFN-γ, IL-2, and GM-CSF levels. These findings indicate that GalNAc-modified hypoxic EVs carrying ANXA2 siRNA can inhibit tumor progression and modulate the TME in pancreatic cancer, supporting their potential as a therapeutic delivery platform.

title: The Role of METTL3-Mediated m6A Methylation in Hepatocellular Carcinoma Progression and Treatment.
abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is a major cause of cancer-related mortality worldwide. Emerging evidence has established N6-methyladenosine (m6A) RNA methylation as a key epitranscriptomic mechanism underlying hepatocarcinogenesis. Methyltransferase-like 3 (METTL3), the catalytic core of the m6A methyltransferase complex (MTC), forms a heterodimer with METTL14 and cooperates with auxiliary components of the MTC to deposit m6A modifications that modulate mRNA stability, splicing, nuclear export, and translation. In this review, we comprehensively summarize the current understanding of METTL3 biology in HCC, focusing on its structure, assembly within the MTC, regulation of coding and non-coding RNAs, and its roles in driving key oncogenic signaling cascades, such as JAK/STAT3, PI3K/AKT/mTOR, Wnt/β-catenin, Hippo/YAP, Notch, Hedgehog, and epithelial-mesenchymal transition. In addition, we discussed how METTL3 remodels the tumor immune microenvironment (TIME) by regulating immune responses and metabolic pathways promoting immune evasion and therapy resistance. Therapeutic strategies targeting METTL3-including small-molecule inhibitors, CRISPR-Cas9 approaches, combination immunotherapy, and tumor-selective delivery systems-are discussed together with the challenges that continue to limit clinical translation. Collectively, these findings position METTL3 as a central epitranscriptomic regulator of HCC progression; however, further mechanistic and clinical validation remains necessary to establish its utility as a therapeutic target and prognostic biomarker.

title: Kandinsky: Enabling neighbourhood analysis of spatial omics data for functional insights on cell ecosystems.
abstract:
AIMS: Spatially resolved omics technologies enable investigation of cellular interactions within their local microenvironments (neighbourhoods) directly in situ. Although several computational methods have been developed for neighbourhood analysis, significant limitations remain in how neighbourhoods are defined and interrogated. Here, we present Kandinsky, a toolkit that provides a flexible and versatile framework for defining and analysing cell neighbourhoods.
METHODS: We developed Kandinsky to improve flexibility in neighbourhood analysis and maximise compatibility with a wide range of spatial omics data. We therefore implemented multiple approaches for identifying cell- or spot-based neighbourhoods that serve as input for four analytical modules: differential gene or protein expression analysis, neighbourhood clustering, co-localisation/dispersion, and spatial hot and cold areas. In addition to its core functionality, Kandinsky enables the execution of external tools within the same analytical framework.
RESULTS: We applied Kandinsky to real and simulated spatial datasets to benchmark its performance against existing methods and demonstrate its ability to uncover biologically meaningful spatial interactions. Kandinsky achieved competitive performance in terms of accuracy, memory usage, and runtime. In real datasets, it suggested transcriptional changes associated with acinar-to-beta cell reprogramming in the healthy pancreas; recapitulated stromal, immune, and tumour-associated clusters in pancreatic cancer; revealed the spatial co-localisation of myoepithelial cells with specific breast cancer subpopulations; and confirmed the association between regions of high CD74 expression and immune cell infiltration.
CONCLUSION: Kandinsky is a flexible and versatile toolkit for neighbourhood analysis that facilitates the exploration and interpretation of complex spatial omics data.

title: Liquid‑liquid phase separation and post‑transcriptional regulation intersection: A new paradigm of RNA‑binding protein condensates in hepatocellular carcinoma malignant phenotypes (Review).
abstract: Liquid‑liquid phase separation (LLPS) enables RNA‑binding proteins (RBPs) to assemble into dynamic biomolecular condensates that influence post‑transcriptional regulation. In hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), these condensates may alter RNA processing and stability. They can also influence transcript localization and translational output. Through these effects, RBP condensates may contribute to tumor growth and metastatic progression. They may further support metabolic adaptation, immune evasion and resistance to therapy. The present review focuses on the intersection between LLPS and post‑transcriptional regulation in HCC. In addition, the present review critically assessed current evidence for RBP condensate function and distinguish direct HCC findings from mechanistic extrapolation. Unresolved questions regarding causality and clinical translation were also discussed. This framework may help clarify how condensate biology contributes to HCC and where therapeutic opportunities remain.

title: MRI-Based Radiomics Predicts FAP Expression and Immunosuppressive Tumor Microenvironment in Hepatocellular Carcinoma.
abstract:
PURPOSE: To develop a Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) -based radiomics-clinical model for noninvasive prediction of fibroblast activation protein (FAP) expression in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), and to explore its association with tumor microenvironment (TME) characteristics and potential immunotherapy response.
PATIENTS AND METHODS: This retrospective study included 104 patients with HCC from the Fourth Hospital of Hebei Medical University, 31 external MRI cases from The Cancer Imaging Archive (TCIA), and 363 transcriptomic profiles from The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA). Immunohistochemistry (IHC) assessed FAP expression. Tumor regions were manually segmented, and radiomics features were extracted using PyRadiomics. Multiple machine learning classifiers were used to construct and validate models for predicting FAP expression. Logistic regression was selected for its balanced performance between the training and validation cohorts, with the smallest area under the curve (AUC) difference among the five machine-learning algorithms. A radiomics-clinical combined model was further developed by integrating the radscore with clinical indicators. Radiogenomic analysis explored radscore-related transcriptomic features and immune infiltration characteristics.
RESULTS: In the validation cohort, the AUC values of the intratumoral, peritumoral, and intratumoral + peritumoral radiomics models were 0.757, 0.502, and 0.784, respectively. The intratumoral + peritumoral model also achieved a sensitivity of 0.692 and a specificity of 0.788, indicating the best overall discriminatory performance among the three models. The radiomics-clinical combined model integrating the systemic immune-inflammation index (SII), prognostic nutritional index (PNI), and radscore achieved an AUC of 0.816 in the validation cohort. Radscore-related transcriptomic modules identified 10 hub genes for risk stratification. Patients in the high-risk group exhibited a more pronounced immunosuppressive TME and poorer predicted benefit from immunotherapy.
CONCLUSION: The MRI-based radiomics-clinical model effectively predicted FAP expression in HCC. Radscore reflected FAP-related immunosuppressive TME remodeling and may provide insights into potential immunotherapy response stratification, which requires further validation in independent immunotherapy-treated cohorts.

title: Single-cell and spatial multi-omics combined with machine learning to unravel the heterogeneity of cholangiocarcinoma and the WFDC3-mediated prognostic regulatory mechanisms.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma (ICC) exhibits substantial cellular heterogeneity and a complex tumor microenvironment (TME), contributing to poor clinical outcomes. Effective prognostic biomarkers and a deeper understanding of the cellular ecosystems associated with high-risk disease remain urgently needed.
METHODS: We integrated five scRNA-seq datasets from GEO with four publicly available spatial transcriptomic sections and bulk transcriptomic data from the TCGA, fu-ICCA, and GEO cohorts. A multidimensional framework combining single-cell analysis, spatial transcriptomics, and machine learning was used to characterize cellular heterogeneity and identify prognostically relevant features. Hotspot was used to characterize T- and B-cell transcriptional modules, Scissor was applied to identify prognosis-associated malignant epithelial cells, and 101 machine-learning pipelines were evaluated to construct the ICCS prognostic signature. Cell-cell communication analysis and exploratory spatial co-density analysis were further performed to characterize ICCS-associated stromal-epithelial interactions, while in silico perturbation and functional assays were used to investigate WFDC3.
RESULTS: The single-cell atlas identified 11 major cell populations and prognosis-associated T- and B-cell transcriptional programs. A six-gene ICCS comprising CEP55, EGLN3, GPRC5A, PRR15, SFN, and WFDC3 showed reproducible prognostic discrimination across the analyzed cohorts. ICCS-High displayed a markedly epithelial-dominant cellular composition, with epithelial cells increasing from 15.47% in ICCS-Low to 78.44% in ICCS-High, whereas T/NK cells decreased from 44.28% to 3.95%. Comparative cell-cell communication analysis revealed prominent mesenchymal-to-epithelial signaling enriched for collagen-related ligand-receptor interactions. COL4A1-CD44 showed the highest relative contribution and a more prominent mesenchymal-epithelial communication pattern in ICCS-High. Exploratory spatial density maps further identified local co-occurrence of mesenchymal and epithelial signals, supporting an ECM-associated microenvironmental context in the high-risk state. Separately, in silico WFDC3 perturbation implicated tumor-related pathways, and WFDC3 knockdown reduced colony formation, migration, and invasion of ICC cells.
CONCLUSION: ICCS stratification captures distinct cellular and molecular states of the ICC microenvironment. The ICCS-High state is characterized by epithelial predominance, reduced T/NK-cell representation, and stronger inferred mesenchymal-to-epithelial collagen-related communication. COL4A1-CD44 and WFDC3 should be regarded as hypothesis-generating biological features requiring further mechanistic validation. ICCS remains a research-stage prognostic signature that requires standardized assays and independent prospective validation before clinical application.

title: Chemokine-receptor axes in immune-tumor cell communication: spatial niches, immune exclusion, and therapy resistance.
abstract: Chemokine-receptor axes are traditionally viewed as leukocyte trafficking cues, but increasing evidence indicates that they also function as spatial and functional organizers of immune-tumor communication. In the tumor microenvironment, chemokine gradients determine which immune-cell subsets are recruited, where they are positioned, and whether they acquire antitumor or suppressive states. This review summarizes experimentally validated chemokine-receptor axes that shape spatial niches, immune exclusion, and therapy resistance in cancer. The CXCL12-CXCR4 axis serves as a prototype of stromal immune exclusion, particularly in pancreatic cancer, where CXCR4 blockade can improve immune accessibility but may require myeloid-directed combinations. CXCR2 ligand axes, including CXCL5-CXCR2 and IL-8/CXCR2 signaling, promote neutrophil-rich suppressive niches, CD8+ T-cell dysfunction, PD-L1 induction, and resistance to immune checkpoint blockade or chemotherapy. The CCL20-CCR6 axis recruits regulatory T cells and contributes to metastatic immune suppression, whereas CCL5-CCR5 signaling organizes perivascular macrophage niches and supports adaptive therapy resistance. CCL2-associated macrophage circuits further link monocyte recruitment, TAM polarization, and immunotherapy responsiveness. We discuss how single-cell and spatial technologies can validate these circuits and guide biomarker-driven therapies. Rather than targeting isolated ligand-receptor pairs, future strategies should reprogram chemokine-controlled immune ecosystems to overcome immune exclusion and treatment resistance.

title: Prognostic Implications of Nitrogen Metabolism-Related Gene SMS in Hepatocellular Carcinoma: An Integrated Bioinformatics and Experimental Research.
abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To identify nitrogen metabolism-related genes associated with hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) prognosis, focusing on spermine synthase (SMS), and to evaluate its prognostic and risk-stratification value.
METHODS: Transcriptomic and clinical data from TCGA-LIHC and GSE14520 and single-cell RNA-sequencing data from GSE242889 were analyzed. Prognostic genes were screened using univariate Cox, LASSO-Cox, and random survival forest analyses. The prioritized candidate, SMS, was subsequently evaluated by immunohistochemistry in an independent cohort of 144 patients with HCC after curative resection. Associations with clinicopathological features, recurrence-free survival (RFS), and overall survival (OS) were assessed. Prognostic models were evaluated using time-dependent ROC analysis, and risk stratification was examined by combining SMS expression with microvascular invasion (MVI) status and Barcelona Clinic Liver Cancer (BCLC) stage.
RESULTS: Integrated bioinformatics and machine-learning analyses prioritized SMS, a key enzyme in polyamine biosynthesis, as the top-ranked nitrogen metabolism-related prognostic candidate, and its prognostic association was validated in GSE14520. In the clinical cohort, high SMS expression was significantly associated with multiple tumors, MVI positivity, and BCLC stage B/C. High SMS expression was also associated with shorter RFS and OS and remained independently associated with unfavorable RFS and OS in multivariable Cox analyses. The combined clinical+SMS model showed better prognostic discrimination than the SMS-only model, whereas its improvement over the clinical model was not statistically significant. Combined stratification showed particularly unfavorable outcomes in patients with high SMS expression and MVI positivity, while SMS further differentiated prognosis within the BCLC A and BCLC B/C subgroups.
CONCLUSION: This study provides independent clinical validation of the prognostic relevance of SMS in HCC. High SMS expression was associated with aggressive clinicopathological features and unfavorable postoperative outcomes. Integrating SMS expression with MVI status and BCLC stage may provide complementary information for postoperative risk stratification.

title: A Hypoxia and EMT-Related Gene Signature for Predicting Prognosis and Immunotherapy Benefit in Hepatocellular Carcinoma.
abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT) and hypoxia are key factors in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) metastasis and recurrence. This study explored their combined impact on HCC prognosis and immunotherapy benefit.
METHODS: TCGA, ICGC, and GEO (GSE14520) datasets were analyzed. An EMT-hypoxia prognostic model (EHPM) was built using LASSO, trained on TCGA (n = 365) and validated in ICGC (n = 231) and GSE14520 (n = 221). ROC curves assessed accuracy. ssGSEA and TIDE explored EHPM-tumor immune microenvironment relationships and predicted immunotherapy benefit. Nine EMT/hypoxia-related genes were validated by qRT-PCR in eight paired HCC and adjacent normal liver tissues.
RESULTS: The 9-gene EHPM was stable across cohorts. The 1-, 2-, and 3-year AUCs were 0.82, 0.72, and 0.76 in TCGA; 0.717, 0.701, and 0.651 in ICGC; and 0.681, 0.609, and 0.557 in GEO. High-EHPM patients showed advanced TNM stage (p = 0.003), poorer differentiation (p = 0.003), higher vascular invasion (p = 0.002), elevated AFP (p < 0.001), shorter overall survival (TCGA and ICGC: p < 0.0001; GEO: p = 0.013), and immunosuppression. EHPM was an independent prognostic factor (HR = 3.315, 95% CI 2.501-4.215, p < 0.001). TIDE indicated more immune non-responders in the high-EHPM group (p < 7.9e-07), As this is based on computational inference rather than treated patients, it should be regarded as hypothesis-generating. The nomogram predicted OS with AUCs of 0.825, 0.734, and 0.777 at 1, 2, and 3 years. qRT-PCR confirmed upregulation of all nine genes in HCC tissues.
CONCLUSION: This EMT-hypoxia model effectively predicts OS and may help identify HCC patients likely to benefit from immunotherapy, though this requires validation in ICI-treated cohorts.

title: Autonomous AI research agents in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma immunology: from multimodal evidence to experimental validation.
abstract: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) remains one of the most challenging malignancies due to profound biological heterogeneity, complex stromal organization, and limited responsiveness to current immunotherapies. Recent advances in single-cell sequencing, spatial omics, digital pathology, and multimodal profiling have revealed that PDAC immune states are shaped not only by cellular composition but also by spatial organization, treatment context, and patient-specific evolutionary trajectories. However, the increasing complexity and fragmentation of biomedical evidence create substantial challenges for conventional artificial intelligence (AI) approaches that are typically optimized for predefined analytical tasks. Autonomous AI research agents represent an emerging paradigm that extends beyond predictive modeling by integrating scientific reasoning, retrieval of heterogeneous biomedical knowledge, computational tool orchestration, workflow adaptation, and evidence traceability. In this Review, we examine how agentic AI systems may contribute to PDAC immunology research, from characterization of immune ecosystems and spatial cellular interactions to biomarker discovery, neoantigen prioritization, and experimental protocol design. We distinguish AI agents from conventional task-specific models and discuss essential capabilities required for reliable biomedical research, including planning, tool use, verification, memory, provenance tracking, and human oversight. Despite promising technical demonstrations in biomedical domains, direct evidence supporting fully autonomous AI-driven discovery and validation in PDAC remains limited. Therefore, we propose a disease-oriented evaluation framework emphasizing benchmark task design, appropriate human and computational comparators, reproducibility assessment, and experimental validation. Future PDAC-specific AI research agents should prioritize evidence-aware reasoning, multimodal integration, calibrated uncertainty, and transparent computational-experimental workflows. Such systems may ultimately accelerate mechanistic discovery and precision immunology, while maintaining rigorous standards for biological validity, reproducibility, and responsible scientific practice.

title: NOL11 is a novel prognostic biomarker associated with immune infiltration and tumor progression in hepatocellular carcinoma.
abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) remains a highly lethal malignancy, and the lack of reliable biomarkers for prognosis assessment and therapeutic guidance continues to limit effective clinical management. Nucleolar protein 11 (NOL11), an important regulator of ribosomal biogenesis and cellular homeostasis, has remained to be fully characterized in HCC. The present study aimed to systematically investigate the expression pattern, prognostic significance, immune relevance and biological function of NOL11 in HCC using transcriptomic and clinical data from The Cancer Genome Atlas, together with in vitro functional assays. NOL11 was significantly upregulated in HCC tissues and was associated with advanced clinicopathological features and poor overall survival. Immune infiltration analysis revealed that NOL11 expression was correlated with distinct immune cell populations, particularly macrophage subsets, and functional enrichment analysis indicated involvement in tumor-related pathways, including the PI3K-Akt and MAPK signaling pathways. In addition, an eight-gene prognostic risk model based on NOL11-related genes was established using LASSO Cox regression, which effectively stratified patient survival and served as an independent prognostic factor. High-risk patients exhibited elevated tumor mutational burden and increased expression of immune checkpoint molecules, including programmed cell death 1 and cytotoxic T-lymphocyte antigen 4, suggesting potential relevance to immunotherapy responsiveness. Furthermore, NOL11 knockdown significantly inhibited HCC-cell proliferation, migration and invasion in vitro. Collectively, these findings suggest that NOL11 plays an important role in HCC progression and tumor immune microenvironment remodeling, and that the NOL11-related risk model may serve as a useful prognostic tool, highlighting NOL11 as a potential biomarker and therapeutic target in HCC.

title: Bulk and single-cell analysis of FAM72D reveals its prognostic and functional relevance in hepatocellular carcinoma.
abstract: Family with sequence similarity 72 member D (FAM72D) has been implicated in proliferative programs in several malignancies, but its clinical significance, cellular distribution and underlying biological programs in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) remain insufficiently characterized. FAM72D expression and its clinical relevance were evaluated using The Cancer Genome Atlas-liver hepatocellular carcinoma (TCGA-LIHC) cohort and three independent GEO cohorts. Cox regression, patient-level bootstrap validation, calibration analysis and decision curve analysis were used to assess its prognostic contribution. Single-cell and spatial transcriptomic analyses were performed to define the cellular distribution of FAM72D. Differential-expression, functional-enrichment, protein-protein interaction and SCENIC analyses were used to characterize FAM72D-centered transcriptional programs. Immune-related analyses were conducted using tumor immune estimation resource and tumor immune dysfunction and exclusion (TIDE) and the functional effects of FAM72D silencing were examined in HuH7 cells. FAM72D was consistently upregulated in HCC tissues in TCGA and three independent GEO cohorts and was associated with adverse clinicopathological characteristics. Higher FAM72D expression was independently associated with unfavorable overall survival in the multivariable TCGA model (hazard ratio 2.02; 95% confidence interval 1.45-2.81; P<0.001). Adding FAM72D increased the optimism-corrected C-index from 0.611 to 0.662, while independent tissue-level validation yielded area under the curve of 0.861, 0.926 and 0.832 in GSE76427, GSE39791 and GSE54236, respectively. Single-cell analysis identified a FAM72D-high malignant-cell population with pronounced G2/M, mitotic, DNA-replication and DNA-repair activity. Bulk and single-cell transcriptomic analyses converged on a coordinated proliferative program characterized by enhanced cell-cycle signaling and forkhead box M1 (FOXM1) regulon activity. High FAM72D expression was also coupled to increased immune-checkpoint expression, reduced estimated CD8+ T-cell abundance and higher TIDE scores. Silencing FAM72D reduced HuH7-cell viability, colony formation and migration and increased apoptosis. FAM72D expression is associated with unfavorable prognosis and a proliferative malignant-cell state in HCC. The combined clinical, transcriptomic, single-cell, immune-related and functional findings support further evaluation of FAM72D as a candidate prognostic marker and a feature of proliferative HCC-cell programs.

title: Progress on therapeutic mRNA vaccines for cancer.
abstract: Therapeutic mRNA vaccines are a clinically validated cancer immunotherapy platform using in vitro transcribed mRNA encoding tumor antigens to induce durable anti-tumor immunity. Advances in mRNA engineering, lipid nanoparticle (LNP) delivery, and immunomodulatory combinations have propelled this approach from preclinical models to randomized trials with survival benefit. This review systematically examines vaccine efficacy through an antigen-delivery-immunomodulation tripartite framework. We trace the evolution from shared tumor-associated antigens to personalized neoantigens identified by computational pipelines, discuss ionizable lipid chemistry and LNP formulation for controlled tissue tropism and transfection, and analyze the bidirectional crosstalk between vaccine components and innate immune sensing that shapes adaptive T cell responses. Clinical evidence across melanoma, pancreatic cancer, non-small cell lung cancer, and other solid tumors is critically evaluated, alongside combination strategies-checkpoint blockade, oncolytic virotherapy, and adoptive cell therapy to overcome TME resistance. Persistent challenges include optimal neoantigen selection, standardized immune monitoring, and predictive biomarkers. We conclude that future research should prioritize systematic optimization of the tripartite design through multi-antigen targeting, tissue-specific delivery engineering, and rational combination immunotherapy, aiming to establish mRNA cancer vaccines as a standard-of-care modality.
